goal: Make MCP failure diagnosis internally consistent across resume safety, reason, recommended action, and Provider account blockers.
acceptance_criteria: A complete current identity-bound pending plan remains resumable when historical drift belongs to another component.
A legacy pending plan with active identity drift remains unsafe and recommends a fresh reviewed run.
Plugin, kernel, and management validations pass without changing generation or delivery authority.
Provider authentication or account availability failures recommend resolving the Provider before resuming the matching safe checkpoint.
resume.safe, resume.reason, and recommended_next_action cannot contradict one another.

quality_metrics.measure: formal provider and delivery route preservation
quality_metrics.target: kernel and provider contract tests pass without a new generation or delivery path
quality_metrics.method: existing kernel and formal provider test profiles

prevention: Confirm acceptance, interfaces, and applicable kernel constraints before implementation.
assurance: Review method, schema, skill, and repository instruction consistency.
Validate that support artifacts cannot authorize formal delivery PASS.
Review changed files against the kernel contract before integration.
control: Run targeted kernel and knowledge tests.
improvement: Record review findings and one bounded improvement experiment.

feedback: Accepted: resume safety, reason, and recommended action now form one coherent decision for identity-bound and legacy checkpoints.

worked: Replaying the exact live diagnosis fixture made the decision-precedence contradiction directly testable.
did_not_work: Historical drift was evaluated before the current identity-bound checkpoint even though resume_safe used the opposite precedence.
experiments: After Provider balance is restored, verify in a new task that cgkn_diagnose_failure recommends resolving the account and then resuming src/service.py.
